title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (20-30Y nominal, 1:40pm ET)
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 Refunding Quarter). As of 2026-09-15 the primary is the REPLACEMENT schedule sb0607 promised, masthead 'For Publication September 9, 2026', re-fetched direct and its text layer independently decompressed this session (plain curl, HTTP 200, 89,250 bytes, md5 c49a5351bf2d31a367817abc62be51bd), superseding the 125,547-byte / md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35 August-5 document the 2026-09-05 initial research read. This row's dates are byte-for-byte identical across the two - announce 10/7/2026, operation 10/8/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 10/9/2026, Liquidity Support, Nominal Coupons 20Y to 30Y, maturity range 10/09/2046 - 10/08/2056, min $0 - but THE MAXIMUM CHANGED, from a flat '$2 billion' to '= or > $4 billion'. Six long-end rows became open-ended in the republication while the front end (10-06 2Y-3Y) stayed at a flat $4 billion. Never quote $2B as the expectation; the operative number prints with the 10-07 announcement, which is also the confirming primary. Stays estimate on two counts that are not date doubt: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and the event-research lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Re-verified at the primary 2026-09-15
notes: IT SHARES ITS DAY WITH treasury-30y-bond-2026-10-08, AND IT STILL CANNOT BID FOR THAT BOND. This is the trap the September pair did not set: on 09-10 the same-day operation was 10-20Y and the maturity range alone excluded CUSIP 912810UW6, but this operation's range (10/09/2046 - 10/08/2056) DOES cover it (matures 2056-08-15), so a reader stopping at the range concludes the opposite of the truth. TreasuryDirect's buyback FAQ excludes on-the-run securities and any not past their first coupon payment date; 912810UW6 fails both on 10-08 (still on-the-run through that morning's reopening, first coupon 2027-02-15). Measured corroboration from fiscaldata's buybacks_security_details across ALL 20 nominal 20Y-30Y operations on record: on-the-run 30Y eligible 0/20, first-off-the-run 0/20, second-off-the-run 20/20 - the pattern is the coupon clause rather than recency. PREDICTED top of this operation's preliminary list: 912810UR7 (2056-02-15) - registered as FT-treasury-30y-bond-2026-10-08-2, scoring off the preliminary eligible-CUSIP list published 11:00am ET 2026-10-07. NO 20-YEAR IS AN ELIGIBILITY QUESTION HERE (added 2026-09-15): the 20-Year reopened 2026-09-15 (912810UX4, $13B, high yield 5.420%) matures 2046-08-15, BEFORE this operation's range starts at 2046-10-09, so it and the 10-21 20-Year are out on range, which needs no FAQ clause to settle. WHAT THE 2026-09-15 PULSE CHANGED, and it supersedes the fill model this note carried on 2026-09-05. (a) The published cap on this row is now '= or > $4 billion', not $2 billion - see source. (b) THE 2026-09-10 10Y-20Y OPERATION UNDER-FILLED: max $6B (tripled), offered $10.489B (cover 1.75x), accepted $5.187B = 86.5%, 23 issues of 40 eligible - the first under-fill in 26 operations in that bucket, and it ran at D+0, 40 minutes after the $22B 30-Year reopening, which is the exact structure THIS event has. So D+0 IS NOT PROTECTIVE and the 09-05 claim that it is (2 of 2) is withdrawn. (c) That under-fill's largest single-CUSIP clip was $1,703M - 11x the <= $150M ceiling the 09-05 shape test assigns to an under-fill - so the shape test's mechanism ('an under-fill is no block cleared') is refuted out of sample; it described a $2B-cap regime this event will not run under. THE MODEL THAT REPLACES IT - two under-fill species, and this corridor's two docs each found one. TYPE 1, the price test: cap far below the book, every clip small, deep miss - this bucket's 2025-11-20 ($0.785B of $2.000B, cover 12.72x) and 2026-03-19 ($0.205B of $2.000B, cover 18.00x). TYPE 2, the cover under-fill: cap lifted above the book, blocks clear freely, shallow miss - 2026-09-10. The 2Y-3Y sibling's cover rule (no operation at a $4B-or-larger cap has ever filled on cover below 2.56x, 0 of 30) governs Type 2 and says nothing about Type 1; the clip test does the reverse. SO 10-08 IS ARITHMETIC ON 10-07'S ANNOUNCED NUMBER, against the last offer book ($19.87B, 2026-08-18): $4B -> 4.97x cover, $6B -> 3.31x, $8B -> 2.48x and the call inverts. Registered as FT-treasury-buyback-20y30y-2026-10-08-3, scoring 2026-10-09. ALSO MEASURED 2026-09-15: the offer-book thinning is programme-wide, not a 10Y-20Y quirk - eligible universes are flat at 35-40 CUSIPs in both buckets all year while par offered per eligible CUSIP fell $1,001M -> $262M in 10Y-20Y (Mar->Sep, -74%) and $1,029M -> $552M in 20Y-30Y (Mar->Aug, -46%). And the ~1bp scale read is confirmed on the tape: the programme's largest long-end purchase ever landed 09-10 and the 10Y rose 10bp that session and 23bp on the week, through 5%. Read it, do not trade it: symbols: [], date and cap are estimate.
